da-false-claim.evidence: The proof block (topological-mass-cat-transient-proof.md:16-17) asserts 'the norm of the sum equals the sum of the norms (by disjointness of the supports)'. Disjoint supports give additivity of the trace (the displayed sum), but ‖Σ tr_i‖ = Σ ‖tr_i‖ only holds if all local traces share sign; transient traces are signed, so this norm-additivity step is generally false.
da-false-claim.notes: The lemma statement itself (topological-mass-cat-transient.md:8-12) is only the trace-additivity identity tr(...) = Σ tr_trans(ρ,p_i), which is fine under disjointness. The over-strong norm-equality is confined to the proof's parenthetical; flagged as warn since the stated lemma is not the false part.

da-vacuous.evidence: The Lean (cat_transient_localises_blowup.lean:38-58) models traceTransient, traceLocal, and N as three independent `opaque` reals/functions and asserts traceTransient = Σ_{i<N} traceLocal i with `sorry`. Between opaque, unconstrained objects the statement carries no content beyond the sorry placeholder.
da-vacuous.notes: Disclosed honestly (lean:18-31): the file states the support/disjointness analysis is 'not available in Mathlib' and the sorry is per AGENTS.md §1 with a -- Ref: [manuscript] citation. So it is an honest stated-not-proved placeholder, not an audit-dodge — warn.

da-overclaim.notes: Recommend dropping the norm-equality clause or restricting to a same-sign / orthogonality hypothesis.
